story_type: four people on an upside down hull offshore, boat crew pulls them off one by one
hook: Four people on an upside down boat, four miles out.
narration: Four people were sitting on an upside down boat, four miles out in the Gulf of Mexico.
Their twenty seven foot boat had started taking on water off Siesta Key, Florida.
A boat crew from Coast Guard Station Cortez ran out to find them.
Up close, the hull was rolling in the swell, and every wave washed over it.
All four had life jackets on, which keep a person floating even if the hull rolls out from under them.
One at a time, the crew reached across and hauled them aboard.
By the last pull, the hull was riding lower and lower in the water.
outcome: The Station Cortez crew got all four off safely, then handed them to a Sarasota police boat.
title: Four stuck on an upside down boat
description:
On Oct. 24, 2012, a Coast Guard Station Cortez boat crew recovered four people from the water after their 27-foot boat began taking on water four miles west of Siesta Key, Florida.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 3rd Class Richard Hodgson, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/317788/station-cortez-rescue
